object: sandstone block from the right jamb of a doorway: New Kingdom hieroglyphs on one face, Meroitic on the adjoining face (82 above, then 83, four lines of smaller characters after a clear space of 12 cm)
site: Sai, north end of the island, temple of Tuthmosis III; now in the Khartoum Museum storehouse
notes: Total height 48 cm, width 36 cm; the four lines occupy 18 cm; hand-copied from the original; Pl. V. Griffith: 'Writing of archaic type. Four lines, each presumably complete' (printed as two type lines, no line numbers). In his commentary he prints the title S-l-e-q-e-ñ (Sleqeñ) as 'a civil title in the Karanôg texts'; the type of the text itself has Sl^eqe^Tyi, with te-y-i where his note has ñ. 'tdx^iNtror, Tazakhiñtarêr, must be the name of a prince.' {ıı} is two upright strokes, perhaps a numeral.
